title.narrative: Increased capacities of regional and sub regional constituents to effectively address the challenge of youth unemployment and under employment in Africa

description.narrative:
Africa has the youngest population globally, with an average age of 19 years. By 2050, nearly one in three young people will be from sub-Saharan Africa. The key challenge for youth entering the labour market is the lack of productive and decent employment opportunities. In 2024, the youth labour force in Africa is expected to reach 120 million. Despite an increase in young workers, key labour market indicators have barely improved due to rapid population growth and a lack of inclusive economic growth. Over 26% of young people in Africa are not in education, employment, or training (NEET), with higher rates for young women. More than 90% of young workers are in the informal economy, with extreme working poverty at 29%.
Global megatrends, such as digitalization and the transition to a green economy, present opportunities for job creation. The ILO has identified youth employment as a critical issue and has set policy priorities through key documents like the Youth Employment Action Plan 2020-2030. The ILO, in collaboration with the African Union, developed the YES-Africa strategy, which calls for investment in decent jobs for youth.
The ILO will continue to support regional and sub-regional constituents by launching YES-Africa, establishing new partnerships, scaling up existing initiatives, reinforcing implementation capacities, and linking young people to the Global Coalition for Social Justice. Additionally, the ILO supports the development of the social and solidarity economy (SSE) in Africa, promoting inclusive business models and sustainable development. The African Union's ten-year SSE strategy, supported by the ILO, aims to legitimize and expand the SSE in its Member States.
